place: A small town in Nakuru County, Kenya (a market town in the Rift Valley highlands, like Njoro or Molo)
about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small town in Nakuru County, Kenya, with its source. Each source entry begins with a tag: [OPENED] the figure was read from a primary document or dataset that was opened (named in the entry); [SECONDARY] it rests on a press report or a search summary of an official release, not opened; [MIXED] part of the entry is opened, part is estimated (the entry says which); [PLACEHOLDER] estimated or carried over from another profile's placeholder, with what it was estimated from. IMPORTANT LIMIT: informal and own-account work, which is most of employment in Kenya (about 84% of jobs: KNBS, Economic Survey 2026), is not represented yet. The generator can only place people in shop, factory and construction jobs, or without work, so a town made from this profile has formal-sector-style employment only; farming, trading from a stall, motorcycle-taxi work and other own-account work are missing. Other structural gaps are listed in the report that accompanied this profile. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md). SINCE 2026-10-09 (employment.*): part of this is represented. The profile now states the share of employees' jobs that are registered, and the share and kinds of own-account work; a town made from it has own-account traders (about 19% of people in work) and employers who register about a third of their jobs. Still missing: farming, own-account work other than trade (transport, workshops, services), and work by the day.

sources.names.customs: Recalled, not opened (to confirm). Kenyan custom: a Christian given name, often a vernacular name, and a family name that is commonly the father's given or vernacular name, so a person may carry a family name unlike a sibling's or spouse's: family_name_from 'own'. Given name first. Share of wives taking the husband's name (8500) is a PLACEHOLDER. Titles Mr and Mrs as Kenyan papers print them in English (Ms also used).

sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: PLACEHOLDER bands around one opened mean: rent was 33.3% of renting households' EXPENDITURE in Nakuru County (urban 34.6%, rural 24.5%; Kenya 36.9%) (KNBS, 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey Basic Report, Table 4.2, https://www.knbs.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2023-24-Kenya-Housing-Survey-Basic-Report1.pdf, opened 2026-10-12). No income is surveyed and no distribution is published: the bands (25% under a fifth, 26% a fifth to three tenths, 32% three tenths to a half, 17% over a half) are a placeholder shaped to that mean, and expenditure is read as income. KNOWN INCONSISTENCY, recorded and left (docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, "Homes by income"): this profile's rents by bedrooms are urban flats' (one bedroom 33% of one wage here, two bedrooms 71%, a let house 163%), so the town's own shares at the start sit far above these whoever lives where. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.

sources.tenancy.possession: PLACEHOLDERS: the Rent Restriction Act (Cap. 296) gives the Rent Restriction Tribunal the power to order recovery of possession of controlled dwellings for unpaid rent; no period was retrieved. Distress for rent (a landlord seizing goods through a licensed auctioneer), which is common, is left out. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for this place of how many tenants served with an application for possession answer it in writing or attend; it is the middle of the two figures opened for other places: 43% of hearings with the renter or someone for them in Victoria, 39.3% of tenants present in Cleveland, Ohio). plan_consider 'may' is a PLACEHOLDER: the Rent Restriction Act (Cap. 296) s 14 lets the tribunal refuse an order for possession unless rent lawfully due is unpaid (secondary), and its power to stay an order on terms is recalled, to confirm. 2026-10-16: see tenancy: the Act states no days for arrears, possession or the warrant; all stay placeholders. The note's claim that distress is done through licensed auctioneers is common practice; the Rent Restriction Act requires the tribunal's leave for controlled premises (s 16).

sources.business.trade_credit_days: PLACEHOLDER 30 days, to confirm: the ordinary terms on which a supplier gives a business time to pay for goods delivered. sources.employment.hours: Employment Act 2007 (Kenya): no provision for lay-off or short time; a change to the terms of a contract is made in writing after consulting the employee (s 10(5)) and one imposed over objection risks being an unfair termination (to confirm: none opened; read from search results 2026-10-13, low confidence). Here: with the employee's agreement, nothing owed for the hours cut. The 45-hour ordinary week is a placeholder. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first. 2026-10-16: confirmed from the full text of the Employment Act 2007: it has no provision for lay-off pay or short time; s 10(5): where a stipulated matter changes the employer shall, in consultation with the employee, revise the contract and notify the employee in writing; s 13(1)-(3): written notice of a change in particulars within a month; s 3(6): any agreement to relinquish or vary the Act's terms is void; s 79: each lay-off of a person is notified in writing to the nearest employment office within two weeks, so a lay-off exists in law but its pay and duration are not regulated; s 27: working hours are regulated by the Act and other law, with at least one rest day in seven, and no hours limit (the 52 hours is from the Regulation of Wages Orders, not opened). The reading of 'consent' is upgraded from low confidence; the right of a cut against objection to be an unfair termination rests on case law, not opened.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Employment Act 2007 s 35 (28 days' notice for the monthly paid) and s 40(1) (redundancy: a month's notice to the employee and the labour officer, and severance of not less than 15 days' pay for each completed year of service) (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it. 2026-10-16: the Employment Act 2007 (https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/2007/11, as revised to 2022, opened): s 35(1)(c): a contract with wages paid at intervals of a month or more ends at the end of the 28 days after written notice (shorter pay intervals: the period next following the notice, s 35(1)(b); daily wages: any day without notice, s 35(1)(a)): the 28 days applies to monthly-paid staff only, so is too long for weekly or daily paid, and the table has one band for everyone; s 40(1): redundancy needs written notice to the union and labour officer, or to the employee and the labour officer, not less than a month before, payment of leave in cash, one month's notice or a month's wages in lieu, and severance of not less than 15 days' pay for each completed year of service (the table's rate, the statutory minimum, not the typical: collective agreements often pay more), not applying to insolvency (s 40(2)). A month's notice at redundancy distinct from the general 28 days is not in the table (no field).
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (6.3% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (2.9%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (14.5%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (1.1%). goods: a consumer problem (20.8%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16 (not applied): no Kenyan yearly rate of any of the five kinds, and no complaint count by category, was found (WASREB Impact Report 15 and EPRA statistics give losses of the networks, metering at 95 to 97% and non-revenue water of 43 to 45%, not billing errors). The gazetted minimum wage of a general labourer in Nakuru city is KSh 16,113.75 a month, and of 'all other towns' KSh 8,596.49 (Economic Survey 2026, Table 3.13, unchanged 2024-25; a 12% rise was reported gazetted 29 May 2026, a search snippet); with 65.3% of employees informal, pay below the minimum is common, well above 1.45% a year if counted so: a different construct. pay_short_by_bps: no figure.
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (52.4%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16 (not applied): the Social Assistance Act 2013 (https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/2013/24, opened) requires a refusal in writing with reasons and a right of appeal to the Magistrates Court within 30 days (s 26) and a decision within one month (s 25(4)); a HelpAge brief on the older persons cash transfer (Briefing no. 16, opened) found 5% of recipients in Siaya and Turkana not paid at the paypoint, 22% of them for register problems (about 1.1% of visits: a different event from a refused claim); an exclusion error of about 50% of eligible households under the old poverty targeting (summary only) is a different regime from the universal 70-and-over rule. No error-and-overturn rate exists in what was found; 64 stays a stand-in.

sources.frictions.venues: tribunal_days 53: the median time to hear and conclude a case in the Small Claims Courts, 53 days, to May 2023 (more than 27,000 cases, KSh 4.6 billion of claims) (Judiciary of Kenya, 'Small Claims Court', https://judiciary.go.ke/small-claims-court/, opened 2026-10-16); the Small Claims Court Act No. 2 of 2016 requires a claim to be determined within 60 days of filing (s 34(1)) and judgment the same day or within 3 days (s 34(2)), for claims up to KSh 1 million (https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/2016/2, opened). The tribunal here stands for the small claims court; no time to disposal was found for the Rent Restriction Tribunal or the Business Premises Rent Tribunal (the 2021 Landlord and Tenant Bill proposed three months: a bill, not law). Replaces the placeholder six weeks (42 days). tribunal_fee_hours_of_pay 3: kept. The Act says a nominal prescribed fee; the amounts are in rules not opened, and a secondary source (k24 and a law firm's page, search snippets) gives KSh 200 for claims under 200,000, 400 to 500,000 and 600 to 800,000; KSh 200 over the lowest general labourer's minimum wage in Nakuru city (KSh 16,113.75 a month, about KSh 71.5 an hour; Economic Survey 2026, Table 3.13) is 2.8 hours, so 3 fits the smallest claims and is low for larger ones: SUMMARY-ONLY. answer_days 14: the Social Assistance Act decides a benefit application within one month (s 25(4)): a different thing. uphold_without_proof_bps: PLACEHOLDER; no figure was found.
sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Kenya, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency).
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for Kenya on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. sources.nature.species: [PLACEHOLDER] Real species of the region; the demographic and detection figures are placeholders except where stated. Black-and-white colobus (Colobus guereza matschiei, the Mau Forest guereza; protected; common in forest fragments, 'sometimes at high density' in small disturbed patches: Primate Conservation 29 (2015), 'Distribution and conservation status of the Mount Kilimanjaro guereza colobus'; densities from 20 to over 90 per km2 in other sites, e.g. 94.4 per km2 in Wof-Washa, Ethiopia; here 0.6 per ha, 60 per km2, a placeholder; troops of about eight use 15 ha, a placeholder). Barriers: built and farmland and grassland (an arboreal animal). Grey crowned crane (Balearica regulorum; IUCN Endangered; Kenya's population fell from about 37,000 in 1987 to under 10,000 by 2024: Citizen Digital, Standard Media, the National Museums of Kenya; crude densities of 0.13 to 0.14 per km2 around Nairobi in a 2023-24 study, i.e. 0.0013 per ha; Lake Nakuru and Nakuru County hold some of the largest numbers); wetlands for roosting and breeding, foraging on farmland and grassland: here 0.1 a hectare on wetland and 0.01 on farmland and grassland, home range 40 ha, placeholders; sensitive to wetland pollution, drainage and poisoning. Hadada ibis (Bostrychia hagedash), a common and conspicuous control, densities by cover placeholders. Growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection: placeholders. Rothschild's giraffe (89 counted in Lake Nakuru National Park in 2011-12: PMC5751992) was considered but is a park animal, not a town's edge.

sources.labour_force_participation_bps: [PLACEHOLDER] Placeholder: 70% of adults aged 18 to the retirement age (here 70) are in the labour force, from 67.4% of those 15 and over in 2025 (ILO modelled estimate via Trading Economics; KNBS Quarterly Labour Force Report not opened: to confirm). sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Kenya, national, annual 2021 (the latest year in the file), from a continuous household survey: ages 25 to 54, 86.983%; 55 to 59, 87.44%; 60 to 64, 83.12%; 65 and over, 61.47%. National, not Nakuru (no table by age for the region was found); not checked against KNBS's own table (to confirm). Most older Kenyans work on, much of it own-account and subsistence work, which this definition counts and which the town cannot yet place (see the note on labour_force_participation_bps). How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.

sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 129 KES to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
